text:
In February 2013 we returned again and again to one measure. Twenty-nine of us said "violence against women"; twenty-eight said "violence against women act"; twenty-six said "the violence against women"; twenty-five said "the violence against women act." Sixteen of us said "of domestic violence." These peaked together on February 28. The record names the first among us to say them on January 3: Maxine Waters.

Around February 12 a second cluster formed. Nineteen of us said "state of the union," eighteen said "of the union address," seventeen said "state of the union address." The record dates the first "state of the union" to January 20 and attributes it to John Barrasso.

We report this as we found it: one bill named in four overlapping ways by roughly a quarter of us on a single day, and an address the whole chamber marked in the same week.
